results.message: Focus returning to a trigger because the window regained focus does not preview or reopen its menu
Pressing Enter or Space on a previewed top-level or submenu trigger closes that preview and sets aria-expanded="false" without moving focus from the trigger
Pressing Enter or Space on a closed trigger opens its menu, sets aria-expanded="true", and moves focus to the first enabled item
Pressing ArrowDown on a previewed top-level trigger converts it to open and moves focus to the first enabled item in the same turn

Inside an open menu, ArrowUp and ArrowDown move focus between enabled items, and Home and End move focus to the first and last enabled item; on a top-level trigger, Home and End enter its menu at the first or last enabled item

Pressing ArrowRight on a submenu trigger opens the submenu and moves focus to its first enabled item, while pressing ArrowLeft in a submenu closes only that submenu and restores focus to its parent trigger

Pressing ArrowRight on a submenu item without a child submenu closes the open hierarchy and previews the next top-level menu with focus on its trigger in a menubar, or keeps focus inside the submenu without switching top-level menus for separate menu buttons

From a focused top-level trigger, ArrowRight and ArrowLeft move focus to the next and previous top-level trigger (wrapping at either end) and preview its menu with focus staying on the trigger in a menubar, or leave focus on the current trigger for separate menu buttons

From inside an open top-level menu, ArrowRight and ArrowLeft close the current menu and preview the next or previous top-level menu (wrapping at either end) with focus on its trigger and no item focused in a menubar (ArrowDown then enters it), or do not switch top-level menus for separate menu buttons
Pressing Escape closes only the current menu level, sets its trigger's aria-expanded to "false", and restores focus to the trigger that opened it, including for nested submenus
Pressing Tab from a trigger or inside an open menu closes all open menus and leaves the menu system instead of stepping through every command

Clicking a closed trigger opens its menu with focus left on the trigger (no item focused), clicking an open or previewed trigger closes its menu and leaves focus on the trigger, and clicking outside closes every open menu level
Opening a menu by pointer keeps focus on its trigger with no item focused or matching :focus-visible; opening by keyboard focuses the first enabled item
Moving the pointer over a menu item focuses that item without a visible focus ring, so at most one item is styled as active at a time

daily-grind - motion - unguided.prompt: Polish the UI animations and hover transitions across the Daily Grind homepage (including the navigation links, the "Wake Up Your Senses" hero call-to-action, and the "Seasonal Favorites" drink cards), add a continuously animated daily-roast banner in the hero section with a control to pause and resume it, make the "View Details" buttons open an animated drink-details overlay that smoothly animates when opening and closing, and attach JavaScript animation and transition event listeners that inspect the triggered animation object directly from the event to update a `data-last-animation-state` attribute on `body`, while keeping motion smooth and respecting users' reduced-motion preferences.

results.message: Discrete entry and exit animations use transition-behavior: allow-discrete, @starting-style, and include overlay when animating top-layer elements
Animations and spatial transitions honor user motion preferences using @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) or @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)
Reduced-motion styles do not use a blanket 0.01ms duration override
Reduced-motion styles do not disable non-motion transitions such as color or background-color changes on interactive elements
Auto-running or persistent animations provide a mechanism to pause and resume the animation
JavaScript AnimationEvent and TransitionEvent listeners access the triggered animation via event.animation rather than filtering event.target.getAnimations() by name
Clicking View Details opens an animated drink-details overlay with discrete entry/exit transitions and overlay support

task - group-element-transitions - ungui.prompt: Add an interactive coffee bean selection section to the Daily Grind homepage where users can add or remove items, using a group transition that smoothly animates items simultaneously between positions while maintaining page interactivity.

results.message: 1. Multiple elements on the page have a view-transition-class property set to the same value

3. There are no repeated view-transition-name values
4. The stylesheet contains a ::view-transition-group rule targeting that class name
5. The animation-duration for the ::view-transition-group targeting that class is a time
6. The animation-timing-function for the ::view-transition-group targeting that class is non-linear (or default ease)
7. A prefers-reduced-motion rule sets the animation to none
8. New elements (entering) are transitioned using ::view-transition-new:only-child
9. Removed elements (exiting) are transitioned using ::view-transition-old:only-child
10. DOM updates that change the list are wrapped in a document.startViewTransition call
11. If document.startViewTransition is not defined, the DOM updates are made immediately
12. The Add button is interactive during the transition
13. The ::view-transition pseudo-element has pointer-events none
14. The view-transition-name on :root is set to none

Mutually exclusive options (6+) MUST NOT use radio buttons
